title: Financial abuse of an elder or dependent adult: noncaretaker, above $950
summary: Violating a theft, embezzlement, forgery, fraud or section 530.5 identity-information law involving an elder or dependent adult's property or identifying information. The accused is not a caretaker and must know or reasonably should know the victim is an elder or dependent adult. This branch concerns value above $950. An elder is at least 65; a dependent adult is 18 through 64 with the specified limitations or qualifying 24-hour inpatient care. The underlying offense must also be proved; loss or a family dispute alone is not enough.
penalty: Misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $2,500, or both. Felony alternative: 2, 3 or 4 years under section 1170(h), a fine up to $10,000, or both. The court must consider a no-contact order lasting up to 10 years; counseling may be a probation condition subject to the statutory ability-to-pay protections. These are adult base penalties; restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: The mental state of the underlying offense, plus knowledge or reasonable awareness of the victim's protected status.

title: Theft by an employee or agent: aggregate above $950
summary: Theft from an employer or principal by a servant, agent or employee, with the value aggregated over 12 consecutive months. This choice is bounded to an aggregate above $950. The literal statute and retained instruction say "$950 or more," but section 490.2 ordinarily gives exactly $950 petty-theft treatment. Do not treat exactly $950 as ordinary grand theft. Employment alone does not prove theft, and the underlying theft elements still apply.
penalty: For the ordinary non-firearm grand-theft branch: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h). Section 672 permits a fine up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. These are adult base penalties; restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: The mental state of the underlying theft; the specified employment/agency relationship and aggregation must be proved.

title: Fraudulent sale or transfer of an access card
summary: Selling, transferring or conveying an access card without the cardholder's or issuer's consent, with intent to defraud. Access cards include qualifying account numbers and other means of account access under section 484d. Value concerns the card or information itself, not automatically the amount later obtained using it. The separate four-person/multiple-card branch is not resolved by this choice.
penalty: Ordinary theft valued at $950 or less receives petty-theft treatment: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Section 490.1 permits an infraction with a fine up to $250 when value does not exceed $50 and there is no other theft or theft-related conviction. Specified prior convictions under sections 490.2, 666 or 666.1 can change the result and require separate review; the ordinary ranges are not a ceiling for those allegations. For ordinary non-firearm theft above $950: For the ordinary non-firearm grand-theft branch: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h). Section 672 permits a fine up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. These are adult base penalties; restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.

title: Fraudulent possession of identifying information: prior conviction
summary: Acquiring or retaining another person's identifying information with intent to defraud, with a prior conviction under section 530.5. An arrest alone does not establish the required conviction. Personal identifying information is defined by section 530.55. This is distinct from theft of access-card information; a low dollar value alone does not make it petty theft.
penalty: Misdemeanor alternative: a fine, up to 364 days in county jail, or both. Felony alternative: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h). The statute authorizes a fine without stating its amount; the applicable fine ceiling remains under review, and no generic $10,000 ceiling is assumed. These are adult base penalties; restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Intent to defraud; innocent possession or transfer is insufficient.

title: Transfer of identifying information known to be intended for unlawful use
summary: Selling, transferring or conveying a specific person's identifying information with actual knowledge that it will be used to violate section 530.5(a). That underlying route requires willful obtaining and use for an unlawful purpose without consent. Mere suspicion is not actual knowledge; an additional intent-to-defraud element is not substituted for the statute's actual-knowledge requirement. Personal identifying information is defined by section 530.55. This is distinct from theft of access-card information; a low dollar value alone does not make it petty theft.
penalty: The statute authorizes a fine, 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h), or both. It does not expressly provide the one-year county-jail alternative found in neighboring subdivisions. A fine-only judgment can result in misdemeanor treatment under section 17(b); do not import a neighboring subdivision's jail range. The statute authorizes a fine without stating its amount; the applicable fine ceiling remains under review, and no generic $10,000 ceiling is assumed. These are adult base penalties; restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Actual knowledge of the planned section 530.5(a) use.

title: Multiple claims for the same loss or injury
summary: Knowingly presenting multiple claims for the same loss or injury, including to more than one insurer, with intent to defraud.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3 or 5 years under section 1170(h), and a fine up to the greater of $50,000 or twice the fraud amount. The $950 health-care threshold does not supply a misdemeanor option for this branch. Section 550 requires restitution. Qualifying prior convictions may add punishment or restrict probation; an auto-insurance claim in a designated fraud-crisis area can double an imposed fine. These are adult base penalties; restitution, assessments, enhancements and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowledge and intent to defraud.
